newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's domestic saving remains too low - advise.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's domestic saving remains too low - advise.

text.p: Morocco still suffers from a low rate of domestic saving, despite the strong interest in the stock market, a senior Moroccan official said on Thursday.

Addressing a two-day Mediterranean economic forum here, King Hassan's economic adviser Andre Azoulay said: "The market capitalisation on the bourse rose to 120 billion dirhams ($12.7 billion) in 1997 from 20 billion dirhams in 1992...But unfortunately saving remains low."
According to Azoulay, the saving rate stands at around 16 percent of Morocco's gross domestic product, estimated at 316 billion dirhams at current prices in 1996.
